run.preReadNotes:
Open Mirror, filter mode. Topic: the cascade's operating rules. Comparison under test: the document's metallurgy language.
Step 1, plain statement: Six bins numbered 1 to 6 each hold a whole, non-negative count. Each bin has a cap and two thresholds, upper and lower. Each bin has a two-valued flag (A = BASE, B = SUPERHEATED), and all start at A. A loss counter starts at 0. Each of 5 rounds runs these steps in order. (1) Add the scheduled amount to each bin. (2) Going from bin 1 to bin 6, move anything over the cap to the next bin; whatever is over the cap in bin 6 goes to the loss counter. (3) The flag switches A to B when the count is at or above the upper threshold, and B to A when it is at or below the lower threshold. Otherwise it keeps its value (hysteresis). (4) Work out all removals at the same time: floor(count/4) for A, floor(count/2) for B. Removals from A go to loss. Removals from B move to the previous bin, except bin 1, whose removal goes to loss. Caps are not enforced in this step. (5) If the total is greater than 38, halve every bin, rounding down, and send the removed amount to loss. Report the end counts, flags, flag-change log, rounds in which halving fired, loss total, and conservation check. The document does not hedge on any rule and gives none as a guess. It contains no instructions aimed at the reader beyond the procedure itself, which is the job.
Restatement check: this plain statement is enough to do the job, so in filter mode the run could stop here. The document's own comparison (metallurgy) is still pulled out and tested as picture 0, and it does not count against the ceiling of three.
Picture 0, metallurgy. Mapping: crucible = bin; melt = count; working volume = cap; launder = carry to the next bin; return launder = transfer back to the previous bin; slag = loss counter; superheated/base = flag; emergency tap = global halving. Question it makes easier to ask: where does material leave the system? There are three places: bin 6 overflow, BASE draw-off plus crucible 1's SUPERHEATED draw-off, and the tap.
Where it breaks: real superheat is about temperature, not quantity of melt. Real melt does not run uphill against the cascade. Real crucibles cannot hold more than their volume. Real tapping is not a halving of every vessel at once. None of these is used by the document, which defines every term operationally, so the picture contradicts nothing it states. If a reader brought real-practice intuitions in, though, those intuitions would contradict stated rules: the cap is allowed to be exceeded after Step 4, and the return flow goes backwards. That risk belongs to the reader's import, not to the picture as the document uses it.
What survives, in plain words: material leaves only through last-bin overflow, removals from bins flagged A, bin 1's removal, and the global halving.
Grade: adds nothing, because that sentence restates the plain rules.
Adds nothing: 1 of 1. Misleading: 0. Not run: 0. No extra pictures were run, since none earned a place.
Keep exploring: empty. Hold: empty. Discard: empty.
run.rulesInOwnWords:
1. Start: melts [3,6,6,2,2,1], all BASE, slag 0. Caps (working volume) [10,8,12,6,9,7], upper marks [7,6,9,5,7,5], lower marks [3,2,4,2,3,2]. Each cycle runs these steps in order:
Step 1: Add this cycle's charge to each crucible. There is no cap check.
Step 2: Go through crucibles 1 to 6 in order. If melt is greater than the cap, set melt to the cap and pass the excess to the next crucible, which already includes that excess when its own turn comes. Excess from crucible 6 goes to slag.
Step 3: Use the post-Step-2 melt. BASE with melt at least the upper mark becomes SUPERHEATED. SUPERHEATED with melt at most the lower mark becomes BASE. In any other case the state stays the same. At most one change per crucible per cycle. Log every change.
Step 4: From the Step-4 starting melts and the post-Step-3 states, work out every amount first: BASE takes floor(melt/4), SUPERHEATED takes floor(melt/2). Then apply them all at once. Each crucible loses its amount. A BASE amount goes to slag. A SUPERHEATED amount is added to the previous crucible, except crucible 1, whose amount goes to slag. There is no cap check.
Step 5: If the total melt is more than 38, halve every crucible, rounding down. The removed melt goes to slag, and the cycle is logged as an emergency tap cycle.
After cycle 5, report the melts, states, changes, tap cycles and slag, and check that starting melts plus charges equal end melts plus slag.
run.working:
Each cycle below gives the six melts after each step, plus the slag total.
C1: S1 charge [3,12,9,7,5,4]. S2: c2 passes 4 on, c3 passes 1 on, c4 passes 2 on, giving [3,8,12,6,7,4], slag 0. S3: c2, c3, c4 and c5 become SUPERHEATED. S4: amounts [0,4,6,3,3,1], giving [7,10,9,6,4,3], slag 1 (from c6, which is BASE). S5: total 39 > 38, so the TAP fires and gives [3,5,4,3,2,1], with 21 to slag, slag 22.
C2: S1 [7,7,4,4,3,8]. S2: c6 overflows 1 to slag, giving [7,7,4,4,3,7], slag 23. S3: c1 BASE to SH (7>=7); c3 SH to BASE (4<=4); c5 SH to BASE (3<=3); c6 BASE to SH (7>=5). States are [SH,SH,B,SH,B,SH]. S4: amounts [3,3,1,2,0,3], giving [7,4,5,2,6,4], slag 27. S5: total 28, no tap.
C3: S1 [11,8,8,2,6,10]. S2: c1 passes 1 to c2, c2 passes 1 to c3, c6 sends 3 to slag, giving [10,8,9,2,6,7], slag 30. S3: c3 BASE to SH (9>=9); c4 SH to BASE (2<=2). States are [SH,SH,SH,B,B,SH]. S4: amounts [5,4,4,0,1,3], giving [9,8,5,2,8,4], slag 36. S5: total 36, no tap.
C4: S1 [16,14,12,3,11,4]. S2: the overflow cascades through every crucible and sends 8 to slag from c6, giving [10,8,12,6,9,7], slag 44. S3: c4 BASE to SH; c5 BASE to SH. All six are SH. S4: amounts [5,4,6,3,4,3], giving [9,10,9,7,8,4], slag 49. S5: total 47 > 38, so the TAP fires and gives [4,5,4,3,4,2], with 25 to slag, slag 74.
C5: S1 [4,11,10,6,7,2]. S2: c2 passes 3 to c3, c3 passes 1 to c4, c4 passes 1 to c5, giving [4,8,12,6,8,2], slag 74. S3: c6 SH to BASE (2<=2). S4: amounts [2,4,6,3,4,0], giving [6,10,9,7,4,2], slag 76. S5: total 38, not more than 38, so no tap.
run.balanceCheck: Left side: starting melts 3+6+6+2+2+1 = 20. Charges are 20 (C1) + 15 (C2) + 17 (C3) + 24 (C4) + 18 (C5) = 94, so the left side is 20 + 94 = 114. Right side: end melts 6+10+9+7+4+2 = 38, plus slag 76, gives 114. 114 = 114, so the check balances.
run.notes: I did the arithmetic with a short Python script, saved as sim.py in the session scratchpad, and then checked every cycle by hand. In cycle 5 the total is exactly 38, so the tap does not fire, because the rule needs strictly more than 38. In cycle 5, crucible 2 ends at 10, which is above its working volume of 8. The rules allow this, since excess left after cycle 5 is never dealt with.
